mainTopic: What an adult may testify about from his childhood (כהונה, rabbinic laws, family lineage), and where such testimony is not accepted.
overview: The גמרא continues through the משנה's list of things an adult may testify about from what he saw as a child. It answers a challenge about a slave who reads Torah: only a child sent to school like a son is a sign. It limits the immersion testimony to תרומה דרבנן. It explains that receiving תרומה at the threshing floor counts because the משנה follows רבי יהודה, and it ties his dispute with רבי יוסי to local custom. It reworks רבי אלעזר ברבי יוסי's story so that a צדיק never actually caused a slave to become a כהן. Childhood memory is accepted for בית הפרס and תחומין because they are only דרבנן, but never to take property away from its owner. A ברייתא adds more such cases and shows that רבי יוחנן בן ברוקא disputes only whether a convert or freed slave is believed. The amud ends by explaining the קצצה ceremony and closing the chapter האשה שנתארמלה.

steps.title: End of the challenge: a slave who reads Torah is still a slave
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes quoting a ברייתא: a slave who acts as steward, puts on תפילין in front of his master, or reads three פסוקים in shul is not freed by that.
steps.simpleTranslation: …a steward, or who put on תפילין in front of his master, or who read three verses in the synagogue — he has not gone free.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a ברייתא it began quoting earlier. The ברייתא shows that some slaves can read from the Torah.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה treats 'he went to school' as a sign that a child was not a slave. But this ברייתא describes a slave reading three פסוקים in shul, so slaves seem able to learn Torah too. If so, going to school would prove nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: A steward or manager put in charge of property
תפילין, worn on the arm and head
He did not go out to freedom; he is still a slave

phrases.aramaic: אַפּוֹטְרוֹפּוֹס, אוֹ שֶׁהִנִּיחַ תְּפִילִּין בִּפְנֵי רַבּוֹ,
phrases.english: a steward, or who put on tefillin in front of his master,
phrases.notes: We're joining in the middle. The ברייתא began earlier: a slave whose master made him a steward…

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ שֶׁקָּרָא שְׁלֹשָׁה פְּסוּקִים בְּבֵית הַכְּנֶסֶת —
phrases.english: or who read three verses in the synagogue —
he has not gone out to freedom.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a challenge that began before this section.
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption that going to school shows a child was not a slave.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא shows a slave reading Torah in shul. So slaves can be literate, and school attendance proves nothing.

steps.title: The slave learned on his own; the משנה means a child raised like a son
steps.stepSummary: In the ברייתא the slave learned by himself. The משנה speaks of a child whom the father treated like his own children and sent to school.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, the slave read on his own initiative. When we say it, we mean a case where he treats him the way one treats his children.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. It separates a slave who learned by himself from a child who was sent to school like a son.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא's slave picked up reading on his own; no one sent him to school. In the משנה's case the child was treated like a son and sent to school, which people don't do for a slave. So the school testimony still counts.

keyTerms.meaning: The way one treats one's children

phrases.english: There, it is where the slave read on his own initiative.
When we say it,
phrases.notes: He means our משנה, which counts going to school as a sign.

phrases.english: it is where he treats him the way one treats children.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the ברייתא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A slave reading Torah would mean school proves nothing.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only a child sent to school like a son is meant, and that is not how a slave is treated.
steps.whatToRemember: Being sent to school like a son is the sign, not merely knowing how to read.

steps.title: Immersing for תרומה means only rabbinic תרומה
steps.stepSummary: The testimony that he saw someone immerse to eat תרומה only permits that person to eat תרומה דרבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'To immerse to eat תרומה' — that is, rabbinic תרומה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next item in the משנה and limits how far that testimony goes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This testimony comes from something seen as a child, so it is not fully trusted. Based on it, the person may eat only תרומה that is required by the רבנן. It does not let him eat תרומה that the Torah requires.

keyTerms.meaning: תרומה required only by rabbinic law

phrases.english: To immerse to eat terumah.
In rabbinic terumah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next item in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The immersion testimony allows eating only תרומה דרבנן.
steps.confusionAlert: This does not make him a full כהן for everything. The testimony only allows rabbinic תרומה.

steps.title: Maybe the man at the threshing floor was a כהן's slave
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's next sign, receiving תרומה at the threshing floor, and asks whether he might just be a כהן's slave.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And that he would share with us at the threshing floor.' But maybe he is the slave of a כהן?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next sign in the משנה and challenges it right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A כהן's slave may also eat תרומה. So seeing someone receive תרומה at the threshing floor might not show he is a כהן; he could be a slave who belongs to a כהן.

keyTerms.meaning: Threshing floor, where תרומה was given out
A slave owned by a כהן, who may eat תרומה

phrases.english: And that he would share with us at the threshing floor.
But perhaps he is a priest's slave?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next sign in the משנה and challenges it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's sign of receiving תרומה at the threshing floor.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A כהן's slave also receives תרומה, so the sign does not prove the person is a כהן.

steps.title: The משנה follows the view that a slave gets תרומה only with his master
steps.stepSummary: The משנה follows the opinion that תרומה is not given to a slave unless his master is with him.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned the משנה according to the one who says: one does not give out תרומה to a slave unless his master is with him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by naming which opinion the משנה follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under this opinion, a slave never receives תרומה by himself. So if someone was seen receiving תרומה without a master, he must be a כהן.

keyTerms.meaning: According to the one who says

phrases.english: We learned it according to the one who says
one does not distribute terumah to a slave
unless his master is with him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Linking the משנה to one opinion
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Receiving תרומה might mean he is only a כהן's slave.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה follows the view that a slave never receives תרומה on his own.

steps.title: The ברייתא: רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי argue
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows the source: רבי יהודה says a slave gets תרומה only with his master. רבי יוסי says he can be given it either way.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: one does not give out תרומה to a slave unless his master is with him; these are the words of רבי יהודה. רבי יוסי says: he can say, 'If I am a כהן, give to me for myself; and if I am a כהן's slave, give to me for my master.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to show that the opinion it just named really exists, and that רבי יוסי disagrees with it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה is the opinion our משנה follows. רבי יוסי allows giving תרומה even to a slave who comes alone, since either way he may eat it. Under רבי יוסי, receiving תרומה would not prove someone is a כהן.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught (in a ברייתא)

phrases.english: As it was taught: one does not distribute terumah to a slave

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן רַבּוֹ עִמּוֹ, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה.
phrases.english: unless his master is with him; these are the words of Rabbi Yehuda.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר: יָכוֹל הוּא שֶׁיֹּאמַר:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says: he can say:

phrases.aramaic: אִם כֹּהֵן אֲנִי — תְּנוּ לִי בִּשְׁבִיל עַצְמִי,
phrases.english: If I am a priest, give to me for my own sake,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם עֶבֶד כֹּהֵן אֲנִי — תְּנוּ לִי בִּשְׁבִיל רַבִּי.
phrases.english: and if I am a priest's slave, give to me for my master's sake.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the opinion named in step 5.
steps.raayaObject: That there is an opinion that a slave gets תרומה only with his master.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא recording the מחלוקת of רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי.

steps.title: The argument depends on local custom
steps.stepSummary: In רבי יהודה's place, receiving תרומה was used as proof of lineage. In רבי יוסי's place it was not.
steps.simpleTranslation: In רבי יהודה's place they would raise a person from תרומה to lineage. In רבי יוסי's place they would not raise from תרומה to lineage.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי disagree: each ruled according to the practice in his own town.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Where receiving תרומה was taken as proof of being a כהן, giving it to a slave alone could lead to treating him as a כהן. So רבי יהודה required the master to be there. Where תרומה was not taken as proof, there was no such risk, so רבי יוסי allowed it.

keyTerms.meaning: In his place (his town or region)
They raise up, giving someone a status

phrases.english: In the place of Rabbi Yehuda
they would raise from terumah to lineage.
phrases.notes: Seeing someone get תרומה was enough to treat him as a full כהן.

phrases.english: In the place of Rabbi Yosei
they would not raise from terumah to lineage.

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּמְקוֹמוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי יְהוּדָה הָיוּ מַעֲלִין מִתְּרוּמָה לְיוּחֲסִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reason behind the מחלוקת in step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The disagreement comes from whether the local custom treated receiving תרומה as proof of being a כהן.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהודה worried that a slave given תרומה alone might be treated as a כהן, because in his place receiving תרומה proved lineage.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows why our משנה can count receiving תרומה as testimony about כהונה: it follows רבי יהודה's place, where תרומה was a sign of lineage.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר ברבי יוסי's one testimony
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר ברבי יוסי says he testified only once in his life, and because of it a slave was raised to כהונה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: רבי אלעזר ברבי יוסי said: In all my days I never testified. Once I testified, and they raised a slave to כהונה based on my word.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with a personal story about testimony that made someone a כהן. This sets up the challenge that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Read simply, the story says a court made a slave a כהן because of a great צדיק's testimony. That troubling idea is what the גמרא is about to question.

phrases.aramaic: תַּנְיָא, אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי:
phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Elazar, son of Rabbi Yosei, said:
In all my days I never testified.
One time I testified,
and they raised a slave to the priesthood based on my word.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא about raising someone to כהונה through testimony.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: His single testimony led to a slave being raised to כהונה.

steps.title: Could a צדיק really cause a slave to become a כהן?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the plain reading. If הקב"ה does not let even the animals of צדיקים cause a wrong, surely He would not let a צדיק himself cause one.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'They raised' — could that enter your mind?! Now, if הקב"ה does not bring a stumbling through the animals of צדיקים, all the more so not through the צדיקים themselves!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the plain meaning of the story using a קל וחומר. The answer comes in the next part of the גמרא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: הקב"ה protects even the animals of צדיקים from causing a sin. It is then even more certain that He would not let a צדיק's own testimony make a slave into a כהן. So 'they raised' cannot mean it actually happened.

keyTerms.meaning: A stumbling, a mishap leading to sin

phrases.english: 'They raised' — could that enter your mind?!
Now, if with the animals of the righteous

phrases.aramaic: אֵין הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מֵבִיא תַּקָּלָה עַל יָדָם,
phrases.english: the Holy One, Blessed be He, does not bring a stumbling through them,
the righteous themselves, all the more so!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the plain wording of the story in step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: The word 'they raised' (הֶעֱלוּ) in רבי אלעזר ברבי יוסי's story.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: קל וחומר: if even a צדיק's animals are kept from causing a sin, a צדיק himself surely would not cause a slave to become a כהן.

steps.title: They only tried to raise the slave to priesthood
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא fixes רבי אלעזר ברבי יוסי's words. They only tried to raise a slave to כהונה because of his testimony. He saw something in רבי יוסי's town and reported it in רבי יהודה's town.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, read it this way: they tried to raise a slave to כהונה based on my word. He saw a slave get תרומה in רבי יוסי's town, and he went and testified about it in רבי יהודה's town.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from step 9 by changing the wording. The slave was never actually made a כהן. People only tried to make him one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רבי יוסי's town, giving תרומה to a slave proved nothing about lineage. In רבי יהודה's town, receiving תרומה was treated as proof of being a כהן. So when רבי אלעזר reported what he saw, people almost treated it as proof, but the mistake was stopped. A צדיק never actually caused the wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather; here it brings in a corrected reading
To raise someone to the status of a כהן

steps.whyThisMatters: It keeps the principle from step 9: הקב"ה does not let a צדיק actually cause a wrong.

phrases.english: Rather: they sought to elevate a slave
to priesthood on the basis of my word.
He saw it in the place of Rabbi Yosei,
phrases.notes: He saw a slave being given תרומה. In that town, this did not prove anyone was a כהן.

phrases.english: and he went and testified in the place of Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא: בִּקְּשׁוּ לְהַעֲלוֹת עֶבֶד לַכְּהוּנָּה עַל פִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge of step 9 by changing the wording of step 8
steps.terutzResolutionType: Change in wording (from 'they raised' to 'they tried to raise')
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The slave was actually raised to כהונה because of רבי אלעזר's testimony
steps.terutzMaskana: People only tried to raise him; the mistake did not actually happen

steps.title: Why is he believed about a בית הפרס
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's next case: an adult is believed that a place is a בית הפרס. It asks why.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה also said he is believed that 'this place is a בית הפרס.' What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the משנה's list and asks why a grown man is trusted here about something he saw as a child. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, things seen as a child are not good enough for testimony. So the גמרא needs a reason why the משנה relaxes the rule for בית הפרס.

keyTerms.meaning: A field where a grave was plowed over, so bone pieces may be scattered in it

phrases.english: And that this place is a beit haperas.
What is the reason?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְשֶׁהַמָּקוֹם הַזֶּה בֵּית הַפְּרָס הוּא. מַאי טַעְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the תרומה discussion to the next clause of the משנה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why a grown man's childhood memory counts for בית הפרס

steps.title: בית הפרס impurity is only rabbinic
steps.stepSummary: The answer: the impurity of a בית הפרס is דרבנן, so the חכמים were lenient.
steps.simpleTranslation: A בית הפרס is only impure by rabbinic law.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. He is believed because the whole impurity of a בית הפרס comes from the חכמים, not from the Torah.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For laws that are only דרבנן, the חכמים were willing to accept weaker testimony, such as an adult's childhood memory. The next steps prove that בית הפרס really is only דרבנן.

phrases.english: A beit haperas is rabbinic.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 11
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The impurity of a בית הפרס is only דרבנן, so the חכמים trusted childhood memory for it

steps.title: Proof from blowing away the dust
steps.stepSummary: שמואל rules that a person may blow on the dust of a בית הפרס as he walks. This shows the impurity is only rabbinic.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: a person may blow on the dirt of a בית הפרס and keep walking.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a first proof that בית הפרס is only דרבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Blowing the dust aside to check for bones is a very easy kind of checking. We would not rely on it for a Torah-level impurity. Since שמואל allows it, the impurity must be only דרבנן.

phrases.english: As Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
A person may blow on a beit haperas and proceed.
phrases.notes: He blows the dirt in front of each step, so any bone shows up and he can walk around it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer of step 12
steps.raayaObject: That the impurity of a בית הפרס is only דרבנן
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמואל's ruling that one may blow on the dust and walk on

steps.title: Proof from a trodden-down בית הפרס
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה בר אמי reports in the name of רב יהודה that a בית הפרס people have walked over is טהור. Any bone the size of a barley grain would have been crushed by feet.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב יהודה בר אמי said in the name of רב יהודה: a בית הפרס that has been trampled is pure. Why? Because a bone the size of a barley grain could not have stayed whole without being crushed by feet.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second proof that בית הפרס is only דרבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Calling the place טהור just because people have walked on it relies on an assumption, not on checking. That kind of leniency only fits a rabbinic impurity. So this also shows בית הפרס is דרבנן.

keyTerms.meaning: A bone the size of a barley grain

steps.whyThisMatters: Both proofs show the same idea: the חכמים were lenient with בית הפרס, so trusting childhood memory fits.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַב יְהוּדָה בַּר אַמֵּי מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר:
phrases.english: And Rav Yehuda bar Ami said in the name of Rav Yehuda:
A beit haperas that has been trodden is pure.
What is the reason?
It is impossible for a bone the size of a barley grain
not to have been trodden by foot.
phrases.notes: Once people's feet crush it, the bone is smaller than a barley grain, so it no longer makes things impure.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב יְהוּדָה בַּר אַמֵּי מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second proof for the same answer
steps.raayaObject: That the impurity of a בית הפרס is only דרבנן
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ruling that a trampled בית הפרס is טהור

steps.title: שבת limits are rabbinic for this תנא
steps.stepSummary: The משנה trusts an adult who says 'until here we used to walk on שבת.' The reason is that this תנא holds תחומין are דרבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה also said he is believed to say, 'Until here we would come on שבת.' This תנא holds that שבת limits are rabbinic.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next case in the משנה and explains it right away. He is believed because this תנא holds the שבת walking limits are only דרבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This works the same way as בית הפרס: childhood memory is good enough for a rabbinic law. The word קסבר shows that this depends on the view that תחומין are דרבנן, a point not everyone agrees on.

keyTerms.meaning: שבת limits, the distance one may walk outside the town
He holds / is of the opinion

phrases.english: And: until here we would come on Shabbat.
He holds: Shabbat boundaries are rabbinic.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעַד כָּאן הָיִינוּ בָּאִין בַּשַּׁבָּת. קָסָבַר: תְּחוּמִין דְּרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the same reasoning as בית הפרס for the next clause
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An adult's childhood memory is accepted for Shabbat limits, since this תנא holds תחומין are דרבנן

steps.title: Why is he not believed about a path or eulogy area
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says he is not believed that someone had a path or a place for standing and eulogy here. The גמרא asks why.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said he is not believed to say, 'So-and-so had a path in this place,' or 'So-and-so had a place for standing and eulogy here.' What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה's case where the adult is not trusted and asks why. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the testimony would give someone a right to use another person's land. That is different from the earlier cases, which were about rabbinic laws.

keyTerms.meaning: A place where people stood and sat during a funeral, and gave a eulogy

phrases.english: And he is not believed to say:
'So-and-so had a path in this place,'
phrases.notes: He means a right of way: someone was allowed to walk through another person's field.

phrases.english: 'So-and-so had a place for standing and eulogy'
in this place.
What is the reason?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵין נֶאֱמָן לוֹמַר דֶּרֶךְ הָיָה לִפְלוֹנִי בַּמָּקוֹם הַזֶּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from cases where he is believed to cases where he is not
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why childhood memory is not accepted for land-use rights

steps.title: We don't take money away based on this
steps.stepSummary: The answer: we do not take money or property away from its owner based on testimony from childhood memory.
steps.simpleTranslation: We do not take money out of someone's possession.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that a right of way or a eulogy area is a money matter. Childhood memory is not strong enough to take property away from the owner.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Giving someone a path through a field takes something away from the field's owner. Leniency was only given for rabbinic laws. For money matters, we need full, proper testimony.

keyTerms.meaning: Taking money (or property) out of someone's possession
We do not take it out

steps.whatToRemember: An adult's childhood memory is accepted for rabbinic matters like בית הפרס and תחומין. It is never enough to take money or property away from its owner.

phrases.english: To remove money, we do not remove it.
phrases.notes: Literally 'taking out money we don't take out.' The land stays with its owner.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 16
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Childhood memory cannot take money or property away from its owner

steps.title: A grown child may repeat what his father said about families
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that a grown child is believed to report that his father told him one family is 'pure' and another 'impure.'
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: a child, once grown, is believed to say, 'My father told me: this family is pure, this family is impure.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with more examples of testimony from childhood memory. The first example is a report of what a father said about different families.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה listed a few cases of childhood testimony. This ברייתא adds family status. A person who heard his father judge families as a child may repeat that report as an adult.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The Sages taught.' This introduces a ברייתא.
A child. Here it means someone who heard this as a child and testifies now as an adult.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
A child is believed to say,
phrases.notes: He means someone grown up now, telling us what he heard back when he was a child.

phrases.english: "This is what my father told me:
'This family is pure,'
'This family is impure.'"

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא that adds more cases of childhood testimony, like those in our משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A grown child is believed to report his father's statement about which families are fit.

steps.title: Can a family really be called pure or impure?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects to the wording, because 'pure' and 'impure' do not describe a family.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Pure and impure' — could you really think that?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to question the wording of the ברייתא. It is setting up a fix to that wording.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Purity and impurity apply to people and objects that become טמא. They are not a way to describe a family line. So the words cannot mean what they plainly seem to say.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Would it enter your mind?' This expresses surprise that something could be meant literally.
Pure / impure (in the sense of טומאה)

phrases.english: "Pure" and "impure" — could that enter your mind?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the wording of the ברייתא just quoted.
steps.kashyaTarget: The words 'pure' and 'impure' in the ברייתא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: טומאה and טהרה do not describe the status of a family, so the plain reading makes no sense.

steps.title: It means fit and unfit lineage
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the ברייתא means 'this family is כשר, this family is פסול,' meaning fit or unfit lineage.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it means: 'This family is fit,' and 'This family is unfit.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own question. The ברייתא is talking about whether a family's lineage is fit for marriage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Pure' and 'impure' are read as 'כשרה' and 'פסולה.' So the child is testifying about family status, which matters for marriage and for כהונה.

keyTerms.meaning: Fit, meaning a family of proper lineage
Unfit, meaning a family with a flaw in its lineage

phrases.english: Rather: "This family is fit,"
and "This family is unfit."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the wording problem raised in step 19.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא literally means purity and impurity.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא means fit and unfit lineage.

steps.title: Eating at a קצצה and bringing חלה to a כהן
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: he is believed about eating at a קצצה, and about bringing חלה and gifts to a כהן, but only if he brought them himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: He is also believed to say, 'We ate at the קצצה of so-and-so's daughter to so-and-so,' and 'We used to bring חלה and gifts to so-and-so the כהן.' This applies only to what he did himself, not to what others did.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא goes back to its list and adds two more things a grown child may report. There is a limit: he must have done it himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Taking חלה and gifts to someone shows that person was treated as a real כהן. A child remembers well what he did with his own hands. He is not trusted about deliveries done by someone else.

keyTerms.meaning: A public ceremony announcing that someone married an unfit match
The portion of dough given to a כהן
The gifts given to a כהן

phrases.english: And "that we ate at the ketzatza
phrases.notes: A קצצה was a public ceremony that announced someone had married an unfit match.

phrases.english: of the daughter of so-and-so to so-and-so,"
and "that we used to bring challa and gifts
to so-and-so the priest."
By himself,
but not by means of another.
phrases.notes: He is only believed about deliveries he made himself, not ones he saw someone else make.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of the ברייתא after the wording fix.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: He is believed about a קצצה and about bringing חלה to a כהן, but only for things he did himself.

steps.title: A convert or freed slave is not believed
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא rules that a convert or freed slave is not believed about anything he saw before his change in status.
steps.simpleTranslation: And in all these cases, if he was a non-Jew and converted, or a slave and was freed, they are not believed.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא adds a limit. A גר or freed עבד cannot testify about these matters if he saw them before he converted or was freed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a grown child may report what he saw as a child. This person, though, saw the events while he was a גוי or an עבד, so the ברייתא does not accept his report. The גמרא will explain the reason in step 28.

keyTerms.meaning: And all of them, meaning all the cases just listed

phrases.english: And all of them,
if he was a gentile and converted,
or a slave and was freed —
they are not believed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a limit to all the cases listed so far.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A convert or freed slave is not believed about what he saw before his change in status.

steps.title: No testimony about a path or eulogy place, and a dissenting view
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא repeats that he is not believed about a path or a eulogy place. Then רבי יוחנן בן ברוקא says 'they are believed.'
steps.simpleTranslation: He is not believed to say, 'So-and-so had a path here,' or 'So-and-so had a place for standing and eulogy here.' רבי יוחנן בן ברוקא says: they are believed.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא ends with the land cases from our משנה. Then it records that רבי יוחנן בן ברוקא disagrees, but it does not say with which part.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These land cases match our משנה and step 16. The ברייתא never says which ruling רבי יוחנן בן ברוקא is arguing with. That gap sets up the גמרא's next question.

keyTerms.meaning: A path, meaning a right of way through someone else's field
A place for the standing ceremony and for eulogies at a funeral

phrases.english: And he is not believed to say
"So-and-so had a path in this place,"
"So-and-so had a place for standing and eulogy
in this place."

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן בְּרוֹקָא אוֹמֵר: נֶאֱמָנִים.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan ben Beroka says: They are believed.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵין נֶאֱמָן לוֹמַר דֶּרֶךְ הָיָה לִפְלוֹנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the ברייתא with the land cases and a dissenting opinion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Childhood testimony is not accepted about a path or eulogy place. רבי יוחנן בן ברוקא says 'they are believed.'

steps.title: Which ruling is רבי יוחנן בן ברוקא arguing with?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which clause of the ברייתא רבי יוחנן בן ברוקא disputes.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן בן ברוקא — which part is he talking about?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which earlier ruling רבי יוחנן בן ברוקא is disagreeing with. It is setting up a search through the options.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His words 'they are believed' come right after the land cases. They could go back to an earlier clause instead. The גמרא wants to pin down which one he means.

keyTerms.meaning: 'On which one?' Which clause is meant?

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan ben Beroka — on which clause?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the unclear dissent at the end of the ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which clause of the ברייתא רבי יוחנן בן ברוקא disputes

steps.title: It cannot be the path case, because that would take away money
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the idea that he disputes the last clause, because that would take property away from its owner.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say he is arguing on the last clause, that is taking money away from its owner!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the first option, the path and eulogy case, and rejects it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We learned in step 17 that money or property is not taken from its owner based on childhood memory. Even רבי יוחנן בן ברוקא would agree to that. So he cannot be arguing about the path case.

keyTerms.meaning: 'If you say.' This introduces a possibility that will be tested.
Taking money or property away from its owner

phrases.english: If you say he is on the last clause:
that is taking money away!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests and rejects the first possible answer to step 24.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The idea that the dispute is about the path or eulogy case
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Accepting the testimony there would take property from its owner, which childhood testimony cannot do.

steps.title: He is arguing about the convert and freed slave
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that רבי יוחנן בן ברוקא disputes the earlier clause and holds that a convert or freed slave is believed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, he is on the earlier clause: 'In all these cases, if he was a non-Jew who converted or a slave who was freed, they are not believed.' רבי יוחנן בן ברוקא says: they are believed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 24. The dispute is about whether a גר or freed עבד is believed. The גמרא quotes that clause again to show where the dissent belongs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling in step 22 is not universal. רבי יוחנן בן ברוקא holds that a convert or freed slave is believed about what he saw before. This is not a money case, so nothing stops him from believing them.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבי יוחנן בן ברוקא lets someone take away a path or field based on childhood memory. His dispute is only about the convert and the freed slave.

phrases.english: Rather, he is on the earlier clause.
"And all of them, if he was a gentile and converted,
or a slave and was freed — they are not believed."

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן בְּרוֹקָא אוֹמֵר: נֶאֱמָנִין.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan ben Beroka says: They are believed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the remaining option after step 25 ruled out the last clause.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יוחנן בן ברוקא disputes the convert and freed slave clause and holds they are believed.

steps.title: What is the reason behind the disagreement?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what principle the two sides disagree about.
steps.simpleTranslation: About what do they disagree?
steps.whatsHappening: Now that we know where the dispute is, the גמרא asks for the reasoning on each side. It is setting up the explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We know what each side rules. The גמרא now asks why one says the convert is believed and the other says he is not.

keyTerms.meaning: 'About what do they disagree?' This asks for the reasoning behind a dispute.

phrases.english: About what do they disagree?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind the dispute identified in step 26.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The underlying reasoning of the תנא קמא and of רבי יוחנן בן ברוקא

steps.title: Did he pay close attention before converting?
steps.stepSummary: The תנא קמא says a non-Jew does not pay close attention to Jewish matters. רבי יוחנן בן ברוקא says that someone planning to convert does pay close attention.
steps.simpleTranslation: The תנא קמא holds: since he was a non-Jew, he did not pay careful attention. רבי יוחנן בן ברוקא holds: since he was planning to convert, he certainly paid careful attention.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the two sides. They disagree about whether the convert noticed these Jewish matters carefully back when he was not yet Jewish.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is how reliable his memory is, not whether he is a valid witness today. The תנא קמא says these things did not matter to him then, so he did not notice them carefully. רבי יוחנן בן ברוקא says he was already planning to convert, so he paid close attention.

keyTerms.meaning: The first, unnamed opinion in the ברייתא

steps.whatToRemember: Childhood testimony is never enough to take property away. The only dispute is about the convert and freed slave: did they pay close attention to Jewish matters before their status changed? The תנא קמא says no; רבי יוחנן בן ברוקא says yes, since they planned to join.

phrases.english: The first tanna holds:

phrases.aramaic: כֵּיוָן דְּגוֹי הוּא, לָא הֲוָה דָּיֵיק.
phrases.english: Since he was a gentile, he did not pay careful attention.
And Rabbi Yochanan ben Beroka holds:
Since his intention was to convert,
he certainly paid careful attention.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנָּא קַמָּא סָבַר כֵּיוָן דְּגוֹי הוּא לָא הֲוָה דָּיֵיק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 27 by giving each side's reasoning.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They disagree about whether a non-Jew who later converts paid careful attention to Jewish matters before his conversion.

steps.title: What does the word קצצה mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the term קצצה, mentioned in the ברייתא, means.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is קצצה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the strange word קצצה means. This question sets up the next step, where a ברייתא will explain it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא listed קצצה as one of the things a grown-up can testify about from what he saw as a child. The word is not obvious, so before moving on, the גמרא stops to define it.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally a 'cutting off.' A public ceremony where a family separates itself from a relative's unsuitable marriage

phrases.english: What is 'ketzatza'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the discussion about the convert and asks about a different term from the same ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The definition of the term קצצה.

steps.title: The Barrel-Breaking Ceremony
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא describes קצצה: when a family member marries an unsuitable woman, the family breaks a barrel of fruit in the public square and announces that his descendants must not mix with theirs. This is the קצצה a child is believed to testify about.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the Sages taught: How is קצצה done? If one of the brothers married a woman who is not fit for him, the family comes, brings a barrel full of fruit, and breaks it in the middle of the town square. They say: 'Our brothers, the house of Israel, listen! Our brother so-and-so married a woman who is not fit for him, and we are afraid his children will mix with ours. Come take a sample for yourselves as a reminder for future generations, so his children will not mix with ours.' And this is the קצצה that a child is believed to testify about.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question by quoting a ברייתא that describes the קצצה ceremony step by step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ceremony is built to be public: a broken barrel, scattered fruit, and a loud announcement to all of Israel. Its purpose, as the family says, is to warn future generations not to mix with this man's descendants. The ברייתא ends by saying this is the קצצה a child may later testify about.

keyTerms.meaning: A sample or sign, something to remember by

steps.whatToRemember: קצצה is a public ceremony where a family breaks a barrel of fruit in the square to separate itself from a relative's unfit marriage. A child who saw it may testify about it as an adult.
steps.whyThisMatters: It defines the קצצה mentioned in step 21, so we know what the grown child is testifying about: a public warning that a relative's marriage was unfit.

phrases.english: As the Sages taught: How is ketzatza done?
One of the brothers who married
a woman who is not fit for him —
the family members come
and bring a barrel full of fruit
and break it in the middle of the square,
and they say: Our brothers, the house of Israel, listen!
Our brother so-and-so married
a woman who is not fit for him,
and we are afraid
that his descendants may mix with our descendants.
Come and take for yourselves
a sample as a sign for the generations,
phrases.notes: People grab the scattered fruit, so the crowd and the story get remembered.

phrases.english: so that his descendants will not mix with our descendants.
And this is the ketzatza
that a child is believed to testify about.
phrases.notes: He saw it as a child, and he testifies about it once he is grown.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the question of step 29 by quoting a ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: קצצה is a public ceremony of breaking a barrel of fruit in the square to announce the family's separation from a relative's unfit marriage. This is the קצצה that a child is believed to testify about.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing the Chapter of the Widowed Woman
steps.stepSummary: The closing formula marking the end of the chapter האשה שנתארמלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, chapter 'The woman who was widowed.'
steps.whatsHappening: This line is not part of the discussion. It marks the end of the chapter האשה שנתארמלה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The הדרן is a traditional closing that expresses our wish to come back and learn this chapter again. It is named after the chapter's opening words.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you (said when finishing a chapter)
'The woman who was widowed,' the name of the chapter

phrases.english: We will return to you,
the chapter 'The woman who was widowed'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the chapter after the final explanation of קצצה.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The chapter האשה שנתארמלה is complete.
